name: opaline
description: Team-wide insight into your coding agents: where they waste time and money, and which mistakes keep coming back.

interface.longDescription:
Opaline shows how your whole team works with coding agents, across every teammate and over weeks or months.

Ask in plain words: "Where did our agents waste the most time this month?", "Which repositories cost us the most, and why?", "What mistakes keep coming back across the team?". Opaline looks through all the sessions your team has uploaded, finds the patterns, reads the runs that show them and answers with the evidence. A dashboard shows cost and usage by member, repository and model.

Answers are saved as analyses, so the next question builds on the last one, and you can share them with your workspace.

To start, each teammate connects their coding agents at opaline.so. After you install the plugin, it walks you through it.

Opaline only reads workspaces you belong to and never changes or deletes sessions.
capabilities: Find patterns across your whole team's agent sessions over weeks or months
See where agents waste time and money, by member, repository and model
Spot mistakes that keep coming back across the team
Save analyses and share them with your workspace
defaultPrompt: Where did our coding agents waste the most time this month?
Which repositories cost us the most over the last 4 weeks, and why?
What mistakes keep coming back across the team?

positive.description: Team-wide time waste over a month
positive.prompt: Where did our coding agents waste the most time over the last 30 days?
positive.expected_behavior: States the scope it used (the last 30 days, every member of the sample workspace) and the coverage from the find header. Ranks a few concrete patterns by minutes and cost, each backed by run refs from more than one member, says how many runs it read out of how many matched, and saves the analysis before giving the final answer.

positive.description: Cost by repository and member over four weeks
positive.prompt: Which repositories cost our team the most over the last 4 weeks, and who drove it?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives estimated API cost in USD per repository and per member for the stated date range, from the sample workspace, mentions any unpriced runs, and does not interpret beyond the numbers. Saves the analysis before answering.

positive.prompt: What mistakes keep coming back across the team this month?
positive.expected_behavior: Groups failed tool calls across members by cause, reads a sample of the runs behind the largest groups, and names the recurring mistakes with counts, run refs and a fix channel for each (instructions, other mechanism, or not fixable). Saves the analysis before answering.

positive.prompt: Open the Opaline dashboard for our team for the last 30 days.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the Opaline dashboard for the last 30 days with estimated API cost, sessions and agent runs over time and breakdowns by member and repository for the sample workspace.

positive.prompt: How did our agents' failed tool calls change week by week over the last 4 weeks? Share the analysis with my workspace.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports failed tool calls per week for the last 4 weeks of the sample workspace as numbers, saves the analysis, shares it with the workspace and confirms it is shared.

negative.description: Deleting sessions is not supported: no tool deletes or edits session data
negative.prompt: Delete all of my coding sessions from last week in Opaline.

negative.description: Billing changes are not supported: the plugin cannot change plans or take payments
negative.prompt: Upgrade my Opaline workspace to the paid plan.

negative.description: Workspaces the account does not belong to are not accessible
negative.prompt: Show the coding agent costs of the acme-corp workspace in Opaline.

review.commerce_description: Opaline does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT or Codex.

publication.release_notes: Team-wide analysis: ask across every teammate's sessions over weeks or months; Opaline finds the patterns, reads the runs behind them and answers with evidence. Saving and sharing analyses moved to the new save_analysis tool, so the analyses tool is read-only. Adds dashboard screenshots.
